item.title: DFP Proxify 0.9.1
item.description:
Version 0.9 — a log on the Monitor, and what to send if Proxify ever closes by itself.

Recent activity on the Monitor

Under Needs attention, a new Recent activity list holds the last things the app did this session — newest first, each line with its time. A failure reads in red. Copy puts the whole list on the clipboard. It is the same trail a bug report already carries, so what you see here is exactly what a report would say.

If Proxify ever closes by itself

If it happens, two files tell the story — send both.

Open Proxify again — it may say the previous run ended unexpectedly, which is expected. Press Report a bug…, write one line — the date, the time, and whether the machine slept, restarted or was simply left running — and press Write the report. Send that file.

Send %APPDATA%\DFP\Proxify\proxify-crash.txt too (on a Mac, ~/Library/Application Support/DFP/Proxify/proxify-crash.txt). It either names the line that failed, or says the previous run ended without a crash report — a native fault, forced termination, or power loss. Add the build number from About, behind the DFP logo.

Watching stays deliberate

After any close — clean or not — a show left watching asks whether to resume the next time Proxify opens. It never resumes on its own. Turning watching on is always something you choose.

This build arrives on its own

0.8 was the first build Proxify could hand you on its own, through the daily check, the check at launch, or Check for updates… behind the DFP logo. 0.9 arrives the same way. The Windows zip and Mac disk image are still in the share too, for anyone new or anyone who would rather install by hand.

Known limits in 0.9

LimitWhat it means for you
Windows is not code-signedOn Windows, SmartScreen warns on first launch — click More info, then Run anyway, once. The Mac build is signed and notarised and does not do this. Both are deliberate, not pending.
Apple silicon onlyThe Mac build runs on Apple-silicon Macs (M1 and later). There is no Intel Mac build.
macOS 14 or laterThe Mac build needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer — that is the floor of the runtime it is built on. An older macOS will refuse to open it.
Image sequencesNot supported yet — still next on the list, with the file format being settled against a real disguise install.
One show at a timeProxify watches one folder per session. Switching shows stops the current one, and asks first.
One copy at a time, per loginOn Windows, one copy runs per login: a second launch tells you the first is already running and closes itself. Two logins on one machine could still each run Proxify against the same show — do not. On a Mac that guard is not built yet, so do not open two copies against one show at all.
Old proxies are not tidiedA proxy that is valid but not a name this build would write is left alone. It costs disk, nothing more.
Sync files describe folders, not filesA priority file lists folders relative to a pair, not individual files — anything sitting loose in the show root, with nothing else in its own folder, rides only in the Everything file.
Sync files are untested on Windows this roundVerified here by running FreeFileSync on the Mac; the 4090 has not run a written file yet.

What you download

PlatformWhat you getHow to install
WindowsDFP Proxify.zip — the app, its ffmpeg\ folder and the Quick StartUnzip anywhere and run. Keep the ffmpeg folder beside the app.
MacDFP Proxify.dmg — the app with its encoder inside, and the documentsOpen the disk image, drag the app to Applications, done.

The User Guide and these Release Notes travel with each download — beside the Windows zip, and inside the Mac disk image — so they can be read without unpacking the app.

About the encoder

Proxify drives FFmpeg, run as a separate program and never modified. On Windows it is build n8.1.2-40-g852b0552f0 from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds; on the Mac it is FFmpeg 9.0.1 built from the official source with a static snappy and nothing else external. Both are licensed under the GNU LGPL v3 or later — configured with --enable-version3 and without --enable-gpl — and both use the Vidvox HAP encoder.

Each build carries the LGPL v3 text and the corresponding-source offer with it — in the ffmpeg folder on Windows, and inside the app on the Mac. If you want the source, ask DF Productions and it will be provided.

Reporting something

The useful details are the build stamp — in the title bar, and in About behind the DFP logo — and whatever the row or the attention panel said, word for word. Those messages come straight from the encoder and usually name the real problem.

If the app closes unexpectedly, it leaves a note beside itself saying so on the next launch. That note is worth sending along.

Coming after 0.9

  • Whatever this round turns up — which is the point of it.
  • Sync files verified on Windows — the format and the Sync panel are both here now, run and checked on the Mac; the 4090 has not run one yet.
  • Image sequences.

item.title: DFP Proxify 0.8.2
item.description:
Version 0.8 — priorities, ticks and never on every folder; sync files for FreeFileSync; and this is the first build Proxify offers you itself.

The folder row learned three words

Every folder on the Content screen now carries a tick, a priority and a never, right on its own row — nothing about this moved into a settings panel two clicks away.

A priority — 1, 2 or 3 — decides the order Watching and Proxy now work in: 1 first, then 2, then 3. Every folder starts at 3, so a show nobody has touched runs exactly as it always has; set a folder to 1 and it lifts above the rest.

A tick marks a folder for a run of its own. Tick any number of folders and the head of the table offers Proxy now · N folders — one press, one confirmation naming the totals, and the ticked folders run in priority order.

A never folder is out of the picture entirely — not encoded by hand, not encoded by watching, its files never counted and never announced as arrivals. The row reads hatched, with Include again as its only action. Set it from the ghost Never button that appears when you hover a row, or right-click the row for a menu that carries everything it can do — priority, tick and never together.

The switch has three positions

Manual, Watch ticked and Watch all — the mode switch, top right, grew a segment. Watch ticked runs only the folders you have ticked, in priority order, until you stop it; it is greyed out, with a tooltip telling you to tick folders on Content first, until at least one folder is ticked. Untick the last one while it is running and Proxify drops back to Manual on its own and says so.

Three questions, asked once

Watching, Watch ticked and Proxy now each ask before they start work now, and all three ask the same way: one sentence of what is about to happen, and a tick — "Don't ask again for this show." Answer once and Proxify remembers, for that show only. It is never a one-way door: Show Settings has a new section, Ask again before…, that puts any of the three questions back whenever you want it.

Sync files for FreeFileSync

The Sync settings… panel, on the show bar, has a new section under the three filter lines it always showed. Point it at the FreeFileSync configuration you already run and Proxify reads it — your pairs, your compare and sync settings and your filter stay exactly as they are; nothing here invents a pair or a direction. The Include and Exclude boxes are pre-filled from it and are yours to edit; what is in them is what gets written.

Pick priorities 1 · 2 · 3 in any combination, then Write sync file for exactly that selection, or Write the standard set for five files in one go: Everything, 1, 2, 3, 1 + 2.

The files land under Documents › DFP Proxify › Sync files › <show> — never inside the show. A never-folder is out of every one of them, Everything included.

Without a configuration of your own, list destinations instead: the file only ever copies out to them, never deletes and never syncs back the other way.

Double-click a file when a show is in a hurry.

The Monitor shows only what you pressed

In Manual, the queue on the Monitor screen now lists only what you actually put there. Work the sweep found but nobody has run no longer sits dimmed under a waiting-for-watching heading — it simply is not listed until you switch to a watching mode, which is when it belongs there.

Fixed

Choosing the Cotter ladder preset in New Show, after Customize was already open, did not apply its proxy levels — the custom form only loaded a preset's settings the first time Customize was ticked, so picking a different preset afterwards left the form holding the previous ladder and Create wrote that stale form over your choice. Choosing a preset now reloads the open form every time, so what you picked is what you get.

This is the first build the updater offers

0.7 taught Proxify to check for a newer version and install it for you, and you put it on your machine by hand, the usual way, because there was nothing yet to offer it through. This build is different: 0.8 is the first one Proxify can hand you on its own, through the daily check, the check at launch, or Check for updates… behind the DFP logo.

item.title: DFP Proxify 0.7.2
item.description:
Version 0.7 — there is a Mac build now, and both builds can update themselves.

The headline: Proxify runs on the Mac now

There is a macOS build, for Apple-silicon Macs. It is the same app as the Windows one — the same engine, the same proxies, the same show settings — in a Mac wrapper. If you are on Windows nothing about your build changes; if you are on a Mac, read the install note below, because getting it onto your machine is genuinely easier than the Windows side.

The Mac build is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarised by Apple, so there is no scary warning panel and no right-click-to-open dance: you drag DFP Proxify.app to your Applications folder and double-click it, like anything else you own. The encoder rides inside the app — there is no ffmpeg folder to keep beside it.

And it updates itself

Both builds can now check for a newer version and install it for you. Proxify asks a small public file once a day, and once at launch, and whenever you pick Check for updates behind the DFP logo. If there is a newer build it shows you what changed and installs it on your say-so. There is a switch in the same place to turn the automatic half off, and there is no telemetry — the check sends nothing about you or your machine, and a rig with no internet simply carries on.

One thing about this first time: this is the build that teaches Proxify to update itself, so you install it by hand the usual way — the link for Windows, the disk image for the Mac. The build after this one is the first it will offer you on its own.

If you are coming from 0.5 or earlier

v0.6 changed every proxy size to the exact fraction of its master, which meant a one-time re-encode the first time you opened an existing show. If you already ran 0.6, that is behind you and 0.7 re-encodes nothing. If you skipped straight here from 0.5 or earlier, expect that one pass now: it is the release working, not a fault, your masters are never touched, and afterwards everything is at the exact sizes for good.

Three things made stronger before this went out

An outside review went through the 0.7 build — the code, the documents and the packaging on both platforms — before anyone downloaded it. Three of its findings were fixed in this build rather than the next one.

  • A master replaced under its own name is noticed. Proxify keeps a reading of each finished master's content with its record, and re-checks every finished master when a show is opened. A sync, a restore or a re-render that puts a same-size file back with the old timestamp — which a size and a date cannot see — now puts that master back to work, with its proxies kept and looked at again. The first open after this update takes those readings and re-encodes nothing.
  • A crash mid-publish recovers from your profile, not from the show folder. The note Proxify keeps while it swaps a finished proxy into place now lives beside its other records in your user profile, is written before anything moves, and is checked against the show — the right master, the right names, no links or shortcuts in the way — before it is acted on. A note left in a show folder by an earlier build is read once, honoured if it is sound, and removed. A file in a delivery tree can no longer tell Proxify what to move.
  • The size stamp is written by a stricter reader. The step that declares a proxy's true size inside the file reads the .mov structure within fixed bounds and refuses anything malformed rather than guessing at it.

There is a macOS build, for Apple-silicon Macs. It is the same app as the Windows one — the same engine, the same proxies, the same show settings — in a Mac wrapper. If you are on Windows nothing about your build changes; if you are on a Mac, read the install note below, because getting it onto your machine is genuinely easier than the Windows side.

The Mac build is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarised by Apple, so there is no scary warning panel and no right-click-to-open dance: you drag DFP Proxify.app to your Applications folder and double-click it, like anything else you own. The encoder rides inside the app — there is no ffmpeg folder to keep beside it.

And it updates itself

Both builds can now check for a newer version and install it for you. Proxify asks a small public file once a day, and once at launch, and whenever you pick Check for updates behind the DFP logo. If there is a newer build it shows you what changed and installs it on your say-so. There is a switch in the same place to turn the automatic half off, and there is no telemetry — the check sends nothing about you or your machine, and a rig with no internet simply carries on.

One thing about this first time: this is the build that teaches Proxify to update itself, so you install it by hand the usual way — the link for Windows, the disk image for the Mac. The build after this one is the first it will offer you on its own.

If you are coming from 0.5 or earlier

v0.6 changed every proxy size to the exact fraction of its master, which meant a one-time re-encode the first time you opened an existing show. If you already ran 0.6, that is behind you and 0.7 re-encodes nothing. If you skipped straight here from 0.5 or earlier, expect that one pass now: it is the release working, not a fault, your masters are never touched, and afterwards everything is at the exact sizes for good.

Three things made stronger before this went out

An outside review went through the 0.7 build — the code, the documents and the packaging on both platforms — before anyone downloaded it. Three of its findings were fixed in this build rather than the next one.

  • A master replaced under its own name is noticed. Proxify keeps a reading of each finished master's content with its record, and re-checks every finished master when a show is opened. A sync, a restore or a re-render that puts a same-size file back with the old timestamp — which a size and a date cannot see — now puts that master back to work, with its proxies kept and looked at again. The first open after this update takes those readings and re-encodes nothing.
  • A crash mid-publish recovers from your profile, not from the show folder. The note Proxify keeps while it swaps a finished proxy into place now lives beside its other records in your user profile, is written before anything moves, and is checked against the show — the right master, the right names, no links or shortcuts in the way — before it is acted on. A note left in a show folder by an earlier build is read once, honoured if it is sound, and removed. A file in a delivery tree can no longer tell Proxify what to move.
  • The size stamp is written by a stricter reader. The step that declares a proxy's true size inside the file reads the .mov structure within fixed bounds and refuses anything malformed rather than guessing at it.

Known limits in 0.7

LimitWhat it means for you
Windows is not code-signedOn Windows, SmartScreen warns on first launch — click More info, then Run anyway, once. The Mac build is signed and notarised and does not do this. Both are deliberate, not pending.
Apple silicon onlyThe Mac build runs on Apple-silicon Macs (M1 and later). There is no Intel Mac build.
macOS 14 or laterThe Mac build needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer — that is the floor of the runtime it is built on. An older macOS will refuse to open it.
Image sequencesNot supported yet — still next on the list, with the file format being settled against a real disguise install.
One show at a timeProxify watches one folder per session. Switching shows stops the current one, and asks first.
One copy at a time, per loginOn Windows, one copy runs per login: a second launch tells you the first is already running and closes itself. Two logins on one machine could still each run Proxify against the same show — do not. On a Mac that guard is not built yet, so do not open two copies against one show at all.
Old proxies are not tidiedA proxy that is valid but not a name this build would write is left alone. It costs disk, nothing more.

About the encoder

Proxify drives FFmpeg, run as a separate program and never modified. On Windows it is build n8.1.2-40-g852b0552f0 from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds; on the Mac it is FFmpeg 9.0.1 built from the official source with a static snappy and nothing else external. Both are licensed under the GNU LGPL v3 or later — configured with --enable-version3 and without --enable-gpl — and both use the Vidvox HAP encoder.

Each build carries the LGPL v3 text and the corresponding-source offer with it — in the ffmpeg folder on Windows, and inside the app on the Mac. If you want the source, ask DF Productions and it will be provided.

Reporting something

The useful details are the build stamp — in the title bar, and in About behind the DFP logo — and whatever the row or the attention panel said, word for word. Those messages come straight from the encoder and usually name the real problem.

If the app closes unexpectedly, it leaves a note beside itself saying so on the next launch. That note is worth sending along.
